title: Ada and the Sigil
premise: Gideon Almeida, runaway apprentice turned ledger-keeper for a guild that trades in impossible things, is tasked with cataloguing a feral child named Ada who arrives speaking a language older than any kingdom. He discovers her words are living sigils — fragments of a binding spell that once imprisoned an ancient power, and which the guild's masters intend to unravel and sell. Torn between loyalty to the guild that sheltered him and the truth of what Ada's voice will unleash, Gideon flees with her across a fractured realm while the guild's hunters close in. In the end, Gideon must choose: complete the binding at the cost of Ada's memory and freedom, or break it and face the waking war — and he finds a third path, giving his own name to the sigil so Ada can live unbound.
about_author: Zephyrine Quintana is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval grimoires before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about languages, ledgers, and the people history forgets to record.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. We meet him cataloguing a bottled storm for the Vellum Guild, establishing his careful, invisible life and his debt to Master Corvane. A knock at the guild door ends the chapter. Emotional beat: quiet unease beneath routine.

chapters.title: A Child Made of Words
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. A mud-caked girl, Ada, arrives alone, speaking a language no scribe recognizes — until Gideon realizes the words rearrange objects on the shelf. Corvane orders her held for 'assessment.' Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread.

chapters.title: What the Masters Buy
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV, sneaking through the guild's restricted vaults. He finds records of previous 'speakers' — all sold to unnamed buyers, all vanished. He understands Ada is inventory. Emotional beat: betrayal; loyalty begins to crack.

chapters.title: Corvane's Kindness
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Corvane treats Gideon warmly, revealing pieces of their shared past, while privately commissioning a translation of Ada's speech from a disgraced linguist. Emotional beat: the seduction of belonging versus growing suspicion.

chapters.title: The First Sigil
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, fragmentary and sensory. She speaks a word that heals Gideon's scarred hand, then collapses, drained. Gideon realizes her language costs her something. Emotional beat: tenderness and guilt entwined.

chapters.title: Night of the Long Ledger
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. He falsifies the guild's records to mark Ada as worthless stock, buying time. The linguist warns him: her words are pieces of an ancient binding, and someone is paying dearly to collect them all. Emotional beat: point of no return approached.

chapters.title: Running on Borrowed Names
chapters.summary: Gideon and Ada flee the guild by night through the flooded undercity. Hunters called the Quiet Brothers track them by silence itself. Emotional beat: terror laced with exhilarating freedom.

chapters.title: The Hedge-Witch's Grave
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. He returns to his dead master's cottage seeking help and instead finds her final letter: she knew what Ada would be, and warned him never to let the guild hear her speak whole sentences. Emotional beat: grief reframed as inheritance.

chapters.title: Grammar of the Old World
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, clearer now. Through dreams she shows Gideon the war the binding ended — two empires unmade by a spoken god. He grasps that each word she loses brings the thing closer to waking. Emotional beat: awe and mounting dread.

chapters.title: The Market at Veil's Edge
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Seeking passage, they encounter a smuggler, Orla, who recognizes sigil-work and offers help — for a price paid in one of Ada's words. Gideon refuses; Orla follows anyway. Emotional beat: wary alliance formed.

chapters.title: Quiet Brothers
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The hunters corner them at a river ford; Ada speaks a defensive sigil that drowns the pursuit but erases her memory of Gideon's name. Emotional beat: heartbreak — protection exacts intimacy as its toll.

chapters.title: Relearning Him
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Traveling with a child who has forgotten him, he earns her trust again through small kindnesses, telling her invented stories about 'the man who keeps ledgers.' Emotional beat: bittersweet second beginning.

chapters.title: The Buyer Revealed
chapters.summary: Orla's POV. Intercepting a guild courier, Orla learns the buyer collecting Ada's words is Prince Ilvane — heir to a throne built on the binding — who wants the old power as a weapon. Emotional beat: stakes widen from survival to war.

chapters.title: Sanctum of Broken Tongues
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. They reach a monastery of mute monks who preserve forbidden languages. There, Ada nearly completes a sentence — and the mountain groans. The monks expel them. Emotional beat: hope punished; the enemy is time itself.

chapters.title: Corvane Catches Up
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Corvane confronts Gideon alone, offering pardon and purpose: help the guild control the binding rather than let a prince weaponize it. Gideon sees the same corruption wearing a kinder mask. Emotional beat: the loyalty-vs-truth theme crystallized.

chapters.title: The Word That Was Stolen
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Guild agents seize Ada briefly; she feels one of her first words torn out and used — far away, a border fortress burns. Rescued by Orla, she returns hollowed. Emotional beat: rage and grief; innocence lost.

chapters.title: Ledger Closed
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. He burns his copy of the guild's master ledger, severing his last claim to his old life, and confesses everything to Ada — including that he once planned to sell her. Emotional beat: absolution sought, not yet granted.

chapters.title: March to the Mouth of the World
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The company races to the binding-site, a sunken amphitheater where the old god sleeps, as Ilvane's army and the guild converge. Emotional beat: grim resolve; every faction arrives for the same door.

chapters.title: The Sentence Completed
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. At the amphitheater, Ilvane forces the final stolen words together; the binding frays and the ancient power stirs, wearing the shapes of the two dead empires. Emotional beat: climax opens — catastrophe made flesh.

chapters.title: What Gideon Gives
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Unable to restore the binding or destroy it, Gideon speaks his own name into the sigil, anchoring the power with a willing mortal self — the one ingredient no thief could steal. Emotional beat: sacrifice as authorship; love against duty resolved.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Kept Her Voice
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The power sleeps again, bound not by chains but by a remembered name. Ada wakes whole, her language hers alone now, meaningless to buyers. She buries the amphitheater. Emotional beat: mourning transformed into guardianship.

chapters.title: A New Ledger
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, years later. Running a small school for stray children with Orla, Ada teaches words freely and keeps one ledger: names given away, beginning with Gideon Almeida. On the last page, a new entry appears in familiar handwriting. Emotional beat: quiet, earned hope.
